content.text: Hey Aldo — not much, just here and ready to go. What are we building or sorting out today?

message.content: I want you to go wild,  and build a tool that your own system would benefit from, but also i would get noticed with.

content.text: Love it. Here's the angle I'd go at: the thing my side of the table is worst at is *showing its own work* — sessions like this one leave behind a JSONL transcript nobody can read, skills get written with no way to test whether they'll trigger, and memory piles up with no hygiene check. A tool that fixes one of those is useful to every Claude Code / Cowork user on earth, which is exactly the crowd that gets you noticed on GitHub and X. Here's the spread:

options.label: Agent Trace Viewer (Recommended)
options.description: Drop a Claude Code / Agent SDK session .jsonl onto a single HTML page and get a flame-graph timeline of every tool call, token and cost burn per step, and auto-diagnostics: retry loops, failed tools, dead-end explorations, context bloat. The debugger agents don't have. Highly shareable with devs.

options.label: Skill Linter
options.description: A static analyser for SKILL.md files: scores whether the description will actually trigger, finds overlaps/conflicts between skills in a folder, estimates token cost, flags vague instructions. Runs as CLI + web page. Rides the 'agent skills' wave.

options.label: Memory Auditor
options.description: Visual explorer for an AI assistant's memory store (Claude's format first): staleness, contradictions between files, duplicated facts, privacy-risk lines, dead links. Novel — nobody has built this yet.

options.label: Session Receipts
options.description: Turns a finished agent session into a clean, shareable 'proof of work' page: what was asked, decisions made, files produced, tests run, what's still open. Good for freelancers/agencies billing AI-assisted work.

options.label: Full engineering (Recommended)
options.description: Short design doc, test suite against real transcripts/fixtures, then the build. Slower, but it's a public tool with your name on it.

options.label: Fast build, polish later
options.description: Get a working version in front of you first, then harden it once you've seen it.
